title: Rate limit login attempts
description: Adds a sliding-window rate limiter to POST /login, hardens session ids and cookies, and stops leaking which emails are registered.

cards.title: AppConfig.login
cards.summary: New config section for the login rate limit.

cards.title: Default login limits
cards.summary: 5 attempts per 10 minutes, then a 15 minute lockout.

cards.title: Clock
cards.summary: Injectable wall clock so the limiter can be tested.

cards.title: RateLimiter.check()
cards.summary: The core of the change: records an attempt and decides whether it may proceed.

provisionalComment.text: Buckets are only removed by reset() after a successful login. Every failed attempt for a new ip:email pair leaves an entry in `buckets` forever, so an attacker cycling through emails grows this map without bound. Consider pruning buckets whose attempts and lockout have both expired.

cards.title: Rate limiter tests
cards.summary: Covers the limit and the lockout, but not the sliding window expiry.

cards.title: createSession()
cards.summary: Session ids go from 64 to 256 bits of entropy.

cards.title: getSession()
cards.summary: Expired sessions are no longer returned.

provisionalComment.text: An expired session is hidden here but stays in the `sessions` map. Should this call sessions.delete(id) before returning undefined, or is there a sweeper elsewhere?

cards.title: destroyUserSessions()
cards.summary: New helper, not called anywhere in this change.

cards.title: limiterKey()
cards.summary: One shared limiter, keyed by client IP and email.

provisionalComment.text: The key includes req.ip, so an attacker who rotates IP addresses gets a fresh budget for the same account each time. Is a per-email limit also needed? The email is also not normalised, so `A@x.com` and `a@x.com` are counted separately.

cards.title: loginHandler()
cards.summary: Input validation, rate limit check, uniform 401, hardened cookie.

provisionalComment.text: verifyPassword() is skipped when the user does not exist, so unknown emails answer much faster than known ones. The uniform 401 message hides account existence, but this timing difference gives it away again. Verify against a dummy hash when `user` is missing.

cards.title: logoutHandler()
cards.summary: Logout now destroys the server-side session too.
